messages:
eng-oncall-bot: PAGER: model-warmup-failures detected in us-west-2 serving cluster — severity: high. Paging primary on-call...
Jordan: I’m live. seeing a spike of model-init failures: OOM at load + deserialization errors. console shows repeated 'cudaMalloc failed' and 'deserialize: unexpected EOF' during warmup.
Sara: Confirmed. Metrics: model_init_failures 120/min, ~60% of warmups failing. Some containers crash and restart (killed by OOM).
Michael: There’s also a node flap in pool-gpu-8. Node went NotReady -> Ready -> NotReady over 3m. Could be hardware thermal/shutdown or driver fault.
Priya: Customer reports: a few high-tier customers saw 503s/timeout on chat endpoints. CS saying ~8 customers impacted intermittently. Ticket #5472 referenced.
Jordan: Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) Pause warmup on non-critical models 2) Redirect traffic to smaller model variants 3) Drain suspect node(s) 4) Disable compile cache parallelism to avoid memory blasting during JIT. Thoughts?
Sara: +1 to pause warmup. How to pause dynamically? We have a feature flag for warmup: `warmup.enabled` per pool. We can flip it for us-west-2.
Priya: CS: please reduce customer error noise if you can, they’re getting alerts. Even a temporary fallback to cpu-backed or smaller-llm is fine.
Michael: I’ll start node drain for gpu-node-23 and scale the pool by +2 warm spares. Docker logs show `libcudnn` errors right before crash. Might be driver-level.
eng-oncall-bot: NOTE: jordan acknowledged pager at 3667004327.
Jordan: doing sequence: (1) set warmup.enabled=false for pool-us-west-2 (2) add routing rule to fallback to model-redwood-small when model-redwood-large init fails (3) drain gpu-node-23 and cordon.
Sara: I toggled `warmup.enabled=false` on the cluster. Confirmed via config service. Warmup tasks will finish current runs then stop.
Michael: Started drain on gpu-node-23: kubectl cordon gpu-node-23 && kubectl drain gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data. Evicting pods now.
Priya: CS: Notifying affected customers with a heads-up. Message: "We are mitigating an infrastructure incident affecting model loads in us-west-2; fallbacks enabled; intermittent errors may persist for ~30-60m."
Jordan: Also disabling compile threads for JIT on worker containers: set env `JIT_PARALLELISM=1` in the runtime config and rollout. This will slow compile but reduce peak memory pressure.
Sara: Rolling update started for runtime-config without warmup and JIT_PARALLELISM=1. Rolling pods ~25% at a time.
Michael: Observed a drop in OOM kills after initial nodes rotated. init_failures down from 120/min to ~30/min. Deser errors persist but less frequent.
eng-oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied (warmup disabled, fallback routing, node drain, JIT parallelism reduced). Monitoring.
Jordan: For long-term, we need: better progressive warmup (rate-limit concurrent inits), stronger pre-checks for artifact integrity (prevent deserial EOF), and watchdog to detect driver flaps.
Priya: CS: will hold off on customer updates until we have 60m stability. Send status updates at 15m intervals please.
Michael: Next step: schedule a driver update + health-check on drained node. I’ll repro deserialization locally with the artifact store; might be artifact truncation on S3 near-renewal event.
Sara: I’m going to enable verbose deserializer logs for the next 30m (env `DESER_LOG=debug`) on a canary to capture stack traces.
Jordan: Also enabling temporary quota throttle for concurrent model inits: set api-gateway header limit -> `x-init-concurrency=2` for non-enterprise customers. This should reduce storm loading.
Priya: CS: customers acknowledged. One enterprise customer asked for rollback to yesterday's model version; we allowed them to pin to v2026-11 for now.
Michael: FYI found a recurring pattern in logs: `compile_timeout: exceeded 45s` then `OOM during compile`. Reducing JIT threads helps but we should consider switching to precompiled kernels for that model.
eng-oncall-bot: ACTIONS: warmup.enabled=false (us-west-2), fallback routing active for redwood-large -> redwood-small, drained gpu-node-23, JIT_PARALLELISM=1 rollout in progress, DESER_LOG=debug on canary.
Jordan: Assigning owners: Michael -> infra/drain & node repro, Sara -> runtime config & rollout, Michael+Jordan -> artifact integrity probe, Priya -> customer comms.
Sara: Rollout finished for 80% of pods. Error rate down to baseline for chat routes. Still monitoring model-init metric.
Michael: Drained node reports hardware ECC errors in system logs. Filing infra ticket to replace GPU host.
Priya: CS: sending update to customers now: "Mitigations applied; we’ve enabled fallbacks and replaced impacted host; limited customer impact remains for a small subset; ETA next update 15m."
Jordan: Can we run one recovery: re-enable warmup for a single canary pod to validate artifact integrity and compile behavior before global re-enable?
Sara: Doing that now on pod runtime-canary-77. I’ve re-enabled warmup only for that pod and kept JIT_PARALLELISM=1.
eng-oncall-bot: canary warmup started on runtime-canary-77.
Michael: Canary completed warmup successfully with JIT_PARALLELISM=1 and no deser errors. Good sign.
Jordan: Ok plan: keep global warmup disabled, gradually reintroduce warmup with concurrency cap and JIT_PARALLELISM=1, push artifact checksum validator pipeline.
Priya: CS: customers asking about root cause. Recommend statement: transient GPU driver/hardware errors causing OOMs during heavy parallel warmup + some corrupted artifact uploads causing deserialization failures. Workarounds applied.
Jordan: I’ll start the post-incident doc and timeline. Tagging this with incident-lifecycle and scheduling postmortem with infra+runtime+ml teams for 48h.
eng-oncall-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: metrics stable for 45m; impact reduced to zero for customers who reported. Please follow up with postmortem and remediation tasks. :white_check_mark:
Michael: Filed replacement host request and artifact validation ticket (ENG-9482, ENG-9483).
Sara: Adding followups: implement init concurrency limit, add retry/backoff on deserial, add compile-time mem safeguard.
Priya: Closing customer loop now. Thanks team. :pray:
Jordan: Thanks everyone. Stand down unless alerts spike again.
